tips.comment: Two Tempting ran with credit on return at Newbury and now goes back to a track where he’s previously won. He’s only 1lb above his last winning mark and has a handy draw for a front-runner on this turning track.

Was beaten less than a length when finishing second over 7f at Haydock thirteen days ago when returning from six months off. Has placed on two of his three starts here. Should be involved at the finish.

Lightly raced at the track but has a good record here and ran well at Haydock despite being briefly hampered. Ryan Moore takes the ride??'a notable jockey booking. Still lightly enough raced to progress.

PEARL EYE ran well here on the opening day and is worth consideration from a better position in the stalls from the same mark here. Might be up in grade, but we've got a claimer taking further weight off and the extra distance looks another plus for me. Has raced well in the recent past in big field handicaps and could get close here.

Transcending Glory’s lightly raced and comes in with some solid form, including a win and a good second recently. The wide draw makes life harder at Chester, but with Marquand on and more to come, he’s still one to take seriously.

C&D winner last September and though that was on heavy ground and we're good here today yesterday's time over the 7f trip suggested there is enough dig in the ground. Add in the fact there has been watering over the week I think my fancy will be fine and from a plumb draw should go well. Only made debut last March and is a three time winner now all over 7f. Yard has had a couple of winners and a couple of thirds at the meeting here this week and this one looks well overpriced to me. Finished last season with a couple of fair efforts in Listed events and if fit enough on seasonal debut looks a fair each way shout here.

The model I run suggests Cheshire Dancer should be able to get the nose in front for this one. Steps out as one of the youngest horses here but has a joint highest RPR of the field and goes out carrying the least weight here. There is 1 to 1.5 stone difference to the top of the market for the 7f trip. Stall draw of 6 is not ideal but still manageable.

TARKHAN was a winner when reappearing at a similar time last year. That was in a previous campaign abroad and now with Jamie Osborne it is interesting that this trainer does not see fit to claim from his new recruit pitched into a hot handicap from top weight.

The Pouncing Lion ran only once at 2, and that was when finishing 3rd of 7 at Goodwood over 9f on heavy going. Today's step up to 12f will suit much better, and these Ghaiyyath offspring seem to flourish at 3. It's interesting that Ryan Moore is booked.
The race fitness of Ammes could give him the edge over Michael Bell's The Pouncing Lion with both likely to benefit from the longer distance here at Chester.
Has only had 3 runs but has finished 2nd in both of the last 2 starts. Cheekpieces added and jockey booking a positive. Holds an each-way chance.

The Foxes has been kept busy over the winter running at Sha Tin and Qatar after Oisin Murphy won a Listed event on him at Newcastle in November. Oisin has ridden him in most of his races and The Foxes won a Group 2 race in both 2022 and 2023 and he could win another Group 2 here drawn well in stall 1 for a rail position throughout.

Just six career runs for the 4yo and room for plenty more improvement. He’s coming off a 9 month break but he won by 5L on his return last year. Gelded since his last run. No problem with the turning track having previously run well on the AW. He finished his last campaign with a 1 1/2L defeat in a very strong Group 2 contest and he can be a big player in this Group 2 contest.

Wasn't beaten far when finishing third from five over today's trip in France last month when returning from seven months off. Should be fitter today. Has won two and placed in the other four of his last six starts. Yard in good form recently. Should be involved at the finish.

DEEPONE was a juvenile Group 2 winner and although hardly seen since he could still be interesting for his top Irish yard. Having already shown himself effective around a similar type of track back home still a colt this one has surprise potential.

A 4-year-old Irish horse with 2 wins from 4 starts on turf, last seen in March finishing 1st of 18 over 12 furlongs at Curragh on soft ground. Up in distance today with a good chance again for the J P O'Brien Stable, which is in good form, as is top jockey Ryan Moore.

Scored in a Class 2 at Goodwood (2 miles, good ground) by four lengths off a mark of 83 late last season when with James Fanshawe proving himself a top stayer. Since transferring to James Owen excelled in winning his first three starts over hurdles, two impressive wins at Grade 2 level, before only going down by a length to good sorts in the Triumph Hurdle at the Cheltenham Festival. Looks just the sort of dual purpose horse capable of winning the Chester Cup. Well drawn in stall six and still nicely handicapped, low in this handicap off a mark of 89, allotted just 8 stone 8 pounds. Big shout.

Caballo De Mar has been a massive improver winning his last five races, the last four at Southwell and the latest making all over two miles. He is ahead of the handicapper here despite being 24 pounds higher than when winning at Ayr last September.
Coming into form at the right time to make a challenge for this. He looks like he's good to stay the trip, and his form suggests that he will be making a bold bid. EW bet.
A former course and distance winner, runner-up in this race last year, and with a good record at this tricky track, looks good each way appeal with 5 places generally available.

Has a strong record at this track and won this race last year on return, showing he can go well fresh. Claimer takes off a useful 3lb and he's well drawn to repeat if ready to fire. Interesting player.

Race 4 at Chester today is the Chester Cup - Handicap (Class 2) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 3,749 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 7-year-old mare Divine Comedy from the Harry Eustace yard, and will be ridden by Kaiya Fraser. This daughter of Le Havre is a talented sort with a haul of 6 wins, is distance suited, and has the services of regular pilot Fraser, who has won on all of her wins bar the first one. She is suited to all going as well as the all-weather track, and has a handy draw too, which will help in this relatively large field. Must be respected here.

SPIRIT MIXER looks vastly overpriced in the Chester Cup at 20/1 (5 places). Leinster and East India Dock are vying for market leadership, however the former carries a poor FlatStats rating alongside J O’Brien’s 3% SR (A/E 0.31) with handicappers in the UK and the latter has to overcome H Davies’s 9% SR (A/E 0.37) on fancied runners carrying up to 8-12. It’s no secret that favourites underperform in this race so an each way punt has to be on the cards and SM makes the most appeal to me; the son by legendary Frankel won consecutive races here at Chester last season (16f), taking his tally to 3 from 5 at the course. The most notable of those was a C2 success in September, beating Mr Escobar by just a nose but the pair pulling 6l+ clear of the field. The gelding is just 2lb higher in the handicap today, gave a decent enough reappearance run at Newbury last month to blow away the cobwebs and is 2/2 when R Hornby has done the steering.

Admittedly, DAWN RISING is not the stable's first choice here, but with a run back from a break serving as a loosener, we could have an improver here. Gave a very strong account in both the English and Irish Cesarewitch at the end of last season and is lighter in the handicap than the Newmarket run. I'm not worried about the woefully inadequate reappearance run last time out. This one could run much better than the price suggests.

DUKE OF OXFORD has undergone a different preparation ahead of this year's renewal. He was disappointing on the back of a busy build-up in this race last year when relatively well fancied and no doubt the yard are in prime form for his bid this year. The fact yhat he has been campaigned largely on the all-weather tempers enthusiasm slightly , but equally he is not fully exposed on turf and race-sharp now with no stamina issues he could surprise.

Venetia Williams has won this consolation event a couple of times in recent years, so she knows exactly what it takes to win here. So that makes MORNING AIR of interest at a juicy price. This 4-year-old filly has shown some reasonable form in France on the flat and showed well-being when winning a hurdle race in December at Leicester. To be fair, she hasn't shown a lot in 2 subsequent outings but could bounce back if taking a liking to this quirky track.

Warda Jamila was an unfancied 12-1 when 4th of 6 not beaten far at Epsom first time out this season. Oisin Murphy takes over the ride and that race should have brought her on and she could win at Chester on her first visit.

Take Heart lines up at Chester today after a solid sixth at Cork last month, where he wasn’t beaten far. He’s just 3lb higher than his win at Glorious Goodwood last summer and seems to be coming back into form. Looks set to run his race.

Wasn't beaten far when finishing just outside the places in fifth over today's trip at Doncaster in March when returning from almost seven months off and was beaten less than a length when finishing second over the same trip at Epsom seventeen days ago. Yard in good form recently. Should be involved at the finish.

Seemed to appreciate the return to turf and quicker ground when finishing a close-up 5th over a mile at Thirsk last time, having been given plenty to do. The extra distance will help here and looks to hold decent claims.

The model I run suggests Qitaal can get the nose in front over the line first in this race. Qitaal steps out with the highest RPR of the field and goes out carrying the joint lowest weight. It is the only runner on this race card that is a prior course and distance winner and has a decent stall draw in stall no. 2.

Grey Cuban is 2 from 3 at Chester, with both wins over C&D last summer. Latterly beat subsequent two time handicap winner - and very progressive - More Thunder by 4.5L giving him 1lb and that rival is now rated 9lbs higher. Grey Cuban is 9lbs higher himself having won since at Doncaster but had excuses on his final start, beaten 50L when clearly out of sorts, and his reappearance on the AW was never going to show his best. Yard love to have winners at their local track and he still looks well handicapped here and in these conditions.

Sportingsilvermine failed to win in 18 starts in Ireland, but since joining James Owen, he has won both starts. He won at Southwell in March off 71 and followed up at Musselburgh off 73. He appeared to appreciate the good ground there and, just 6 lbs higher, looks to have a great chance of bringing up the hat trick.

Was a major eyecatcher for me last time at Epsom and plugged on nicely to be a close third and if coming on for that looks sure to go close here. Bolted up here over further last season and from a plumb draw if he gets a good early position could well dominate this field. Went well for young apprentice last time and form around tight tracks read well and he must have a huge chance here as will stay on best of all given form over further. Tightly banded handicap this and with rider's 7lb claim I like this one's mark and course form. Should go well.

The model I run simulates this race and has Model Approach coming in first. This result has largely been driven by Model Approach having the joint highest RPR of the field and is well treated at the lower end of the weights. Stall 14 isn't the most helpful, but 1m 4f should be just about a long enough distance that it doesn't cause too much disadvantage.

Woodstock City is not a prolific horse, but he does hold his own as a handicapper. He's dropped to the rating he was last successful at Ripon, and he ran well at this meeting last year, finishing third. His trainer has enjoyed much success at this course/meeting, and he's an interesting runner if on a going day.

Has bags of stamina and won two hurdles this season. Showed retains flat form when only 13 days ago was only narrowly beaten at Ripon. Marquand booked for the ride and should be thereabouts with his known stamina.

Was beaten less than a length when finishing second over 2m at Kempton last month when returning from eight months off and followed up with a win over the same trip at Ripon thirteen days ago beating reopposing Surrey Belle (runner up). Callum Shepherd in good form recently. Should be thereabouts. NAP

Won twice towards the end of last year and although held after, returned last time out from an absence to finish a decent 3rd. Didn't get the clearest run but stayed on well. Step back up in trip will suit.

Finished last year with a win at York in October and followed that with a 2nd place on reappearance at Southwell last month. Disappointed there last time but likely to bounce back and holds an each-way chance.
Law of the Sea has finished placed in his last 2 races over this trip at Chester. He is very well handicapped on the best of his form and looks a strong each way bet at huge odds.

The 8yo wasn’t great in his three AW runs this winter, but he has better stats on turf. He’s coming off a 4 month break and can go well when fresh. His last run on quick turf ground was last August, running to a good level on Shergar Cup day in a much stronger contest than this handicap. He has an 8lb lower mark now and has run well at this track previously.

Won well at Newmarket last month, and the runner-up in that race franked the form when winning next time. Just failed in follow-up bid when nodded on the line and comes here from an unchanged mark from last time. Should win.
How far does he win by? This horse is bred to be a bit special. Horse won last time out in a with finishing sectionals. Been given a break to continue progress, looked big strong and progressing.

Several of these are making their seasonal debut and look opposable, so this race-fit gelding from a red-hot stable could be the e/w value. He ran a cracker on debut as a 3yo last time out when upped in class to stay on into 2nd ahead of some very decent yardsticks. He gets the first-time cheekpieces now, which are a positive on breeding, and trip and ground are ideal, so he's a safe bet to be in the mix here, in my opinion.

Just about an each-way price on his reappearance run here. Showed a decent turn of foot when winning at Southwell on his reappearance run last month, so will be fitter than most. Just as effective on turf, so each-way potential.

Won twice at this trip last year on turf and AW. Won again in February at Wolverhampton. Returned LTO from a little absence to stay on well over 6f at Newcastle. Will be better for that, and Hollie Doyle is an eye-catching booking on board.

Impressive winner at Chester, showing strong early speed and a professional attitude. Took a significant step forward when narrowly beaten into third in a thrilling finish in the Group 2 Coventry Stakes at Royal Ascot, highlighting his class and tenacity. Possibly found the drop back to 6 furlongs at Deauville less than ideal on his final run of the season, failing to reproduce his best form. Returns from a 9-month break and makes his handicap debut, and he remains a respected contender with potential for further improvement as a 3-year-old. Top jockey and trainer combo and has every chance in being in the placings tomorrow.

Won a class 4 maiden over 5f @ Bath as a 2yo and then ran with merit in some Grp class races afterwards. Down in grade in this classs 2 handicap on 3yo return, hood on first time today, good jockey up and in hands of a very good trainer, making current 18/1 decent Ew value in the race.

Stardinia also showed significant promise on debut in a big field (15 runners), finishing second and beaten only half a length. That was in Class 2 company on similar going, and the third from that race has placed again since. She is likely to progress and must be respected.

Could have come up against a decent sort when B/F on their debut in a class 4 novice over 5f @ Bath, coming 2/9 beaten 2.25 lengths. Entitled to come on for that run/experience, good jockey retains ride and very good trainer 23 percent with a Lsp of 26.50 on her 2yo's here last 5 seasons, making current 7.50 very good Ew value in the race.

A Kameko filly, a half-sister to 3 successful winners, including the promising 2-year-old King Cuan, who triumphed at distances of 6f-7f, and the 5f winner Ernest Rutherford. Her Dam was a winner at 7f and 7.6f. This newcomer hails from a stable in excellent form, having celebrated a debut victory with a 2-year-old at Newmarket just last week. At 22/1, this opportunity presents great value.
Well-bred filly out of Sea The Stars, out of a powerful stable with big things ahead of her. Ground conditions today will suit. Stable going well, should be hard to beat.

Did not excell on sole 2yo run, however it was in a very hot class 2 maiden @ Doncaster on soft ground and they were very short in the betting market. Looks the type to improve as a 3yo, step up in trip will suit on nice pedigree, good jockey up and top class trainer who is in form, is 23 percent with a Lsp of 30.67 on his 3yo's here last 5 seasons, making current 7/1 very good Ew value in the race.
Ran freely on debut in November when finishing 7th of 11. Likely to settle better with hood applied and holds an each-way chance if finding improvement.

She showed potential in her debut run at Newbury when she finished 3rd of 6 last October. However, I think the switch to AW and Wolverhampton, which is the trickier AW course, proved too much for her when she finished only 10th of 11 last November. Serious improvements are required now going up in class, but a return to turf might be more beneficial.

Things not quite going to plan and really struggled LTO when 8 of 8 at Doncaster last October. But it helps she has course experience and dropping down 2 classes just might make things interesting and worth finding out with the huge price on offer.

Much better than the bare result last time when finishing down the field on seasonal reappearance. Cruising behind the leaders, but the gaps just not appearing. Comes here fit and well and from an unchanged mark.
Comes into this race in fine form. I think he did well to beat Kodi Lion last time as he slightly reared at the start. Should finish strongly.

Pipped by half a length last time out at Doncaster by 'Dorney Lake' who has to contend with a bigger rise in weight for that victory. Won twice around this time last year, and looks more interesting these days with recent change to a big name trainer.

PHOTOSYNTHESIS can be expected to progress on the back of his first start for over a year last month. The stable he now races for should also have now learned something about him and still just a four year old he can defy his current mark.

Got a bit of trouble in running when 2nd at Southwell last time and switched across the track but only ever put in the race approaching the last half furlong. Well backed that day when on a handy handicap mark and is still competitive today and should be involved in the finish.

Should improve for stable debut over 7 furlongs when runner-up at Doncaster at the end of March following an absence of 246 days. He is a previous winner over 7 furlongs and this drop in trip could pay dividends.

Some respectable form from time in Ireland. On stable debut after a break, she didn’t get a clear run but has potential to bounce back here. The step up in trip looks likely to suit, and she has both distance and going form in her favour.
Unlucky on finals day LTO when nowhere to go approaching the final furlong. Unexposed as a sprinter and comes here from the same mark as last time. Decent chance in this.

Ran well on debut to win over 5f at Yarmouth in October last year and wasn't beaten far when finishing fourth when stepped up to today's trip at Doncaster a fortnight ago when returning from six months off. Yard in great form recently. Should be thereabouts.

Very much unexposed and only makes 3rd start in handicaps. Yard and jockey flying - Ed Walker 25% win strike rate and Hector Crouch is 20% win strike rate. Only run on ground good or better was a 4 length clear cut victory. Gets preferred high draw here at Ascot and good each way value at double figure odds.

Stuck on gamely at Southwell last time for 2nd behind Hammer the Hammer, who has had further success and is obviously well handicapped. Wheels of Fire should be able to get rolling in this race and stay on for at least a place.

Nicely drawn in stall 3. Rossa Ryan (SR 14%) rides for Ralph Beckett (SR 20%). Zoustar gelding who won on debut in June last year but didn't settle to racing after that. Slightly better handicapped on return and fast going should suit. Has potential and its hoped some issues have been fixed in the interim. Interesting on first start back. A possible in a competitive Class 4 3yo handicap over six furlongs.

Last time out, this horse finished 4th at Newbury when getting a run in the middle of the track, where the three that finished in front of him all ran up the rail. I fancy that form is better than it looks.

Was Superb winning debut run at Salisbury, which did not look likely at the beginning of that race, but struggled when switching to AW in handicap debut LTO when only 8 of 9 at Kempton last December. But that was a tricky starting mark, to be fair, so good news: mark has been eased this time out.

This horse was well touted in the market when going off at 8/11 and winning with stacks in hand in a novice race. Crucially that race had an 82 rated horse in it which was receiving 7lb from this one so the fact that NP was such a warm order suggests she's highly likely to be much better than this opening handicap mark of 80. She's clearly thoroughly unexposed and she could well progress again to take this on her way to bigger prizes.
Improved in each of his runs and a respectable run from this mark last time. Needs to improve again to win this and shouldn't be far away.
This one has an each-way shout in conditions that he will appreciate. Ran well on reappearance last time and will come on for that run.

Was going in the right direction, which led to getting rewarded by an impressive win LTO in handicap debut at Nottingham last month. So, raised mark and going up in class means he will need a better performance this time out.
Still in form but was never in a place to challenge last time, having been at the back in a slow-run race. Comes here from the same mark, and with a better pace expected, can go well.

Trainer out of form. Jockey could do with a winner. Wind op on the horse seems to have worked, although 5 years old improvement still possible. Race easily winnable. Apprentice handicap, so dodgy, but Lule Catton highly capable. Sound chance.

Ran well to finish third when stepped up to today's trip at Kempton last month and followed up with a close second (by a short head) over the same trip at Lingfield eleven days later. Has won two and placed in six of his nine starts on turf. Fred Daly's 7lb claim should come in useful. Should be thereabouts.

Two return runs for the 4yo filly. Beaten just over a length last week in a Listed contest despite meeting plenty of trouble in the race. She was beaten by three runners rated 105+. She should be a big player in this handicap while racing off a 94 mark.

Qirat has gone up the weights for finishing 2nd in two competitive handicaps at the end of last season. Both came off proper soft ground, and I think a return to a quicker surface, as well as 7f, will suit him best. He won on reappearance last year and boasts plenty of Ascot form. All the pace looks high, but it should give him a good tow into the race from stall 9, and he can claim this from a mark of 99 before moving onto pattern company as a 4yo.

Unexposed 5yo, 1 win from 6. Irish raider. Trained at a small yard who has great stats this year, 13 winners for a huge 25% strike rate. He was 2nd of 17 last year in a £78K handicap, losing by a hd. Big return run during March when 5th of 27 in the Irish Lincoln - soft ground. He could be better on this quick ground going off a couple of big runs last year. He can improve for his return run, will be fresh after a 2 month break and he has a good jockey booking for this £51K handicap.

Much better on her handicap debut over hurdles, winning with much more in hand than the bare margin suggests. She has only gone up 2lb for that which is very fair and there should be more to come from her.

The model I run suggests Rukaana can win this one. This result has largely been driven by Rukaana having the highest RPR of the field, joint highest official ranking, but doesn't appear to be overly penalized with the weights. Rukaana goes out with the first-time blinkers on, which should aid improvement, and Benjamin Macey on board claims a massive 8 lbs, leaving the net weight being carried over this 2m trip the second lowest of the 10 runner field.

He posted easily his best run to date when weakening into seventh on his handicap bow at Carlisle last month and I just have this sneaking suspicion that they have been biding their time with him. Off 6lb lower here and down in class, the six-year-old should be at peak fitness. This sharp track should suit the son of Hillstar and I've definitely tipped up worse 25/1 shots.
Was a winner at Fakenham over hurdles in March but has not been as good over hurdles or on the flat in 3 races since. Holds an each-way chance if rediscovering that March form.

All Well And Good is ridden by Sean Bowen again, who had two close 2nd places and a win in bumpers on him. But sent over hurdles, his race was all but over early with mistakes at the first three flights at Wetherby in March. Beau Morgan took over last month, and he jumped perfectly when 2nd of 13 at Ffos Las to Ronnies Rules and should win this time against hurdles debutant Howth.

Headed on the run-in over half a furlong shorter at Sedgefield last time out, ridden by a 3-pound claiming apprentice. Could benefit from the return of Brian Hughes to the saddle, who took the ride in the two races prior to that recent race.

The model I run suggests Topofthecotswolds can cause an upset here and get across the line first. Highest RPR of all the runners. Does step out carrying the second highest weight due to having the second highest official ranking, but Ollie Pears has a high RTF% as trainer. Highest Top Speed on the card.

Drops back in distance this time. Going right-handed. Back on a flat track. I felt he ran well last time out. Looked to have every chance 2 fences from home. Just looked to lack match practice. Beaten 11 lengths back in 3rd place. Given that was his first run in almost 5 months, you can forgive that effort. He should be straighter for that run this time around. He does sit on a career-high mark, however, but hasn't had all that many chase runs. The jockey takes off 5 lbs too, which should prove helpful. He ran a nice enough race at this course over hurdles behind Go Chique. Beaten just over 1 length in 2nd place. That race turned into a flat battle with hurdles taken out. He goes well on flat tracks, with all career wins coming on this type of track. If he runs his race, I think he can go close in this company.

The model I run suggests Giovanni Change should win this one. This is a small 5-runner race, but Giovanni Change steps out carrying significantly less weight than the other runners. Lines up here as the only previous runner to have won over this course and distance. This race is virtually 3m, and the weight difference should be telling by the end.
Got up very late to beat a useful horse last time over shorter, and the step up in trip today is sure to suit, giving my selection a good each-way chance.

The model I run suggests an each-way bet on Accidental Legend is the value play here. Accidental Legend has the highest RPR of the 9-runner field and also goes out carrying the least weight of all the runners. Massive odds of 34s, so clearly not fancied by the early market. This horse is the only one on the race card to have victories at this course and distance apart from Hardy Boy. Pulled on the last two outings, but hoping back to some form here and should go close.
Consistent performer who has won on 2 of the last 3 starts, including on stable debut here on the latest outing. Up another 6lb but likely to be there or thereabouts.

Shorter than my usual bets but I backed him last time out when he ran a cracker on ground that was probably softer than ideal. He won a division of this race last year and with Sean on board he is a confident win bet.

I'm opting for the current 2nd favourite here in Chestnut Pete over Williethebuilder, who as I type is still being backed in this morning. He likes it at Hereford, has 10st 2lbs on his back (Shane Quinlan's allowance takes off 3lb).

The model I run suggests an upset here and recommends the value bet being Chanelle Noir. Chanelle Noir is one of the younger runners here and looks the progressive type. 5th in April run but looked like a longer distance would suit, and this trip today represents a step up in trip by 2f.

Musique De Fee found plenty of improvement with the fitting of cheekpieces, with easy wins over course and distance and at Sedgefield in March. She was then second at Newton Abbot last month, and although off a 4 lbs higher mark here, she looks hard to beat.

The model I run recommends the value bet as being Shorten Sassy. Shorten Sassy steps out with the lowest RPR of the field, but not by much, and is more than offset by the large weight differential to the rest of the field. A weight differential of 1 stone and 10 lbs to the top of the market is a fairly large spread, and Shane Quinlan on board relieves a further 3 lbs to take the total weight difference to 2 stone (!) over the 3m1f trip.

The Dream Goes On is the suggested winner by my model. Steps out here with the highest RPR of the field. Has the lowest official ranking, which leaves it with the least weight to carry around this 2m 4f trip. Luke Scott on board relieves a further 5 lbs and should give it the weight differential required to get the job done here. Comes to this in recent form, having won 2 races prior to an unfortunate fall at the last race when looking to make it 3 wins on the spin. Can get the job done here today.

The model I run suggests Captain Attridge can win this one. Lines up for this 6-runner race with the joint highest RPR but only the second lowest official ratings. That suggests the gap between racing potential and penalization through weights is too big (i.e., not carrying enough weight for the potential). A similar case could be made for a few other runners in this category, but Captain Attridge is a previous course winner, has decent form, and by far the highest top speed on the card.

MOONSHINE MAN could be worth the risk up in trip ahead of just his third start in handicap company. He takes in his second run following wind-surgery potentially understanding more as a horse now and he is well enough treated to think he is overpriced tonight.

The model I run suggests Rewired should win this race. Rewired lines up with by far the highest RPR, but the second lowest official ranking. Subsequently, it carries less weight around this 2m trip. Previous winner at this distance and looks to build on the form of prior runs (form reads 0,1,3).
Was beaten less than a length when finishing third over today's trip at Redcar eight days ago when returning from almost four months off. Drawn well in stall one. Should be thereabouts.
Followed three 2nd place finishes with a win at Yarmouth last month. Failed to build on that at Wolverhampton last time, but no surprise to see bouncing back and likely to be there or thereabouts.
Zuffalo has not been in form this season so far but is now below his last winning mark and drops to Class 6 for the first time since its last winning run. All points to being competitive today.

Queen Of Steel’s been flying over hurdles with back-to-back wins and now switches back to the Flat. She’s yet to get her head in front on the level, but she’s in great nick and could run better than her mark suggests if that confidence carries over.

A progressive three-year-old trained by Richard Hannon, River King showed promise on debut and improved to win last time out, indicating a solid upward curve. Well-bred for sprint distances, he travels strongly and finishes with purpose. Likely to improve further, especially over a similar trip on good ground conditions.

Wasn't beaten far on debut when finishing just outside the places in fifth over today's trip at Newbury last month. Should progress further today. Has been gelded since. Should be involved at the finish.
She made some progress LTO when 4th of 7 at Beverley last month, and conditions will be similar. So, I do think provided improvements are made that she has a chance tomorrow.
Struggled in debut run when only 12th of 14 last month. But pretty much the same distance and same class this time out might help. Sometimes, a switch from AW to turf can be beneficial.
Well-bred filly who is still ahead of the handicapper and given a good opportunity here to get on the board before she goes up in the weights next week.

4th last time out, on good/firm conditions. Up in trip for the 1st time at this distance. Had only 2 runs on good/firm, running well on both occasions. 5th placed rival in recent event has since won, on today's conditions and different track. Top speed rate. Sire 'Camelot' shows 17% win rate at this track for 4-year-olds overall. Trainer 20% win rate at this track with 4-year-olds. EW play at these odds looks good.

Trained by Dr Richard Newland, Chess Dad is a lightly raced three-year-old with scope for development. Finished a promising second on debut, showing tactical speed and determination. Drawn well and partnered with Silvestre De Sousa, he should be competitive. Further progress is expected, especially with an ideal trip and ground.

Ran in a listed event last time out. Certainly appears to be the going good/soft for its poor run. Winning Debut recently had 3rd and 4th winning on good ground, including a Class 1 event. Sire form at this track shows an 18% win rate. Trainer win rate with 3-year-olds is 21%. Jockey W Buick has a 21% win rate.

130,000 gns yearling Dubawi colt who holds an entry in the Derby and is obviously held in high regard by his connections and is working out well back home in the James Owen yard was last seen at Southwell 19 days ago where finishing a promising 3rd/8 despite being caught further back than ideal he made a bold move from the rear and showed very good signs of ability now with that run on the all weather under his belt having also learnt plenty from that outing as he is a pretty smart individual and is the type to learn and progress quickly he steps up in trip here also switching to a turf track that being a positive move by his connections and this trip can bring out further improvement and he should take well to the turf this is no horse to underestimate especially as he is in receipt of weight here jockey Daniel Muscut takes the ride and can give Rogue Millions a promising ride here at Nottingham . Respected .

A Kameko gelding, a half-brother to notable winners like Meliora, who triumphed in France over 1 and a quarter miles, and Monna, a German 9 furlongs winner, both of whom have shown their capabilities. He is about to make his debut in a strong novice field but has a reputable stable behind him and the skilled Callum Hutchinson in the saddle. This 3-year-old is a promising contender. At 33/1 odds, an each-way bet is definitely worth considering.

Was well beaten over today's trip at Thirsk seventeen days ago when returning from six months off. Has placed on two of his three starts here. Amie Waugh's 3lb claim should help. Should be involved at the finish.
Bit of an outsider in this field, but top jockey booking with the 7lb claim. I think Saved Lizzie can outrun the odds. Back off a break, and I'm hoping for a fresh and eye-catching run.

A well-bred two-year-old trained by Karl Burke, making a debut at Ripon over 5 furlongs. Shows promise based on pedigree, with a sire known for speed. Drawn in stall 1, which often suits front-runners at Ripon. Market support and Burke’s strong record with juveniles makes this one noteworthy.
Has been disappointing in both starts to date. Should be better than those races have shown and is the only one with any experience in this race. Holds an each-way chance.

ZAPPATA's winning run will obviously end when the handicapper eventually catches up but he just keeps finding races that look pretty easy to pick off. I don't see anything causing the upset in this field.

Is down a pound for reappearance and wasn't far behind for more after being hampered 2f out and still finishing with zest. Is a speedy horse and can come on for the run. Ruth Carr does well with newer horses to the yard. I think this looks all set for a big one.
Fortamour is a standing dish at Ripon and ran a close third on its seasonal debut three weeks ago. Off the same handicap mark, it must be competitive here over its favourite course and distance.

SHOWTIME MAHOMES runs well fresh and the stable also perform well with them rested, so this one is considered back on the turf. Could run well from this mark, even in this grade and is only a couple of pounds above last winning mark. Ran respectably in this race last year from two pounds higher and is considered each-way.

Ex-inmate of Karl Burke and caught the eye on last run last year when an unlucky loser at Chester. Had first run for new connections having been gelded last month, which was his first run for 9 months. Worth an each-way punt as he should improve for that run.

Trained by W J Knight, Dubawi Time is a lightly raced four-year-old stepping into handicaps. Displays tactical speed and stays the mile well. Improving with each run this season and comes off a solid effort in a competitive field. Likely to be suited by the Ripon layout and surface.
Ran on well when winning over a mile at Doncaster 13 days ago and is twice a runner-up over this trip off this mark of 67.
Lightly raced 4-year-old French import. Two UK runs and a little unlucky to lose by a neck two weeks ago over this 10-furlong trip. Good RPR rating posted. Room for improvement.
Should go very well after a decent seasonal debut in a better race and the wrong trip. I'll be surprised if he isn't involved in the finish.

Ex-Irish trained 4yo, 1 win from 4. UK debut four weeks ago after 9 months off the track. Not disgraced over 16f in a competitive handicap, still in the mix late on and not given a hard time. Going off his Irish form, he should be more suited by this 11.5f trip. On a decent mark and Ryan Moore takes over the saddle. The favorite in the race has a 7lb penalty for a win four weeks ago.

Four career runs for the 3yo. Beaten just 3L in a Group 2 on his final start last year. A respectable 4th in a strong Group 3 on his return six weeks ago - two of those rivals have won Group 3 races since. Aidan O’Brien/Ryan Moore team up and should be a big player in this Listed contest.

The 4yo filly was beaten in a £238K US Grade 1 four weeks ago, not much going right for her in the race. She was a runner-up in Group 1 last summer and followed that with a Group 3 win. The return to quick ground will be a big positive for the selection in this Group 3 contest.

Not a favourite horse of mine, but the fact the O'Neill 8yo has dropped 13 lb in 18 months prior to winning last month at Newcastle, his first win since Jan 2022, can't be ignored. He wore cheekpieces for that win for the second time. He ran well when he first wore them at Cheltenham's Showcase meeting last October and retains them for today.

Glory And Fortune wore Helvenin down to win more comfortably than the 0.75L winning distance suggests and can confirm form with that rival on 2lbs worse terms. A mark of 132 is still 11lbs above his mark when winning the Betfair Hurdle back in 2022. Whilst he might be a 10yo, he's suited by these conditions and a big field. With his yard in flying form (37.5% last 14 days) and the prospect of first-time cheekpieces finding further improvement, he still looks well handicapped.

Three runs from the 7yo since Dec, after 19 months off the track. Three narrow defeats while racing in good company. Beaten 1/2L in a 16 runner contest last time out. Good jockey change for this handicap hurdle and he could still have a big run in him.

Two against the field here, and Dr T J Eckleburg looks overpriced for Evan Williams, who has won this prize four times since 2013. Reverts back to hurdles, having spent the last two seasons over fences, but he won at Chepstow two starts back before a really good 5th at the Aintree meeting last time. So this doesn't look like a desperate move but rather a well-thought-out plan. Finished 1st and 3rd on two starts over C&D (both chasing) but may yet have unfinished business over the smaller obstacles - still just a 7yo and in good form. A mark of 125 is the same as his winning chase mark two starts back, and he seems a better, stronger horse going back hurdling.

Daddy Long Legs has only had one previous run on the flat when he finished second at Saint Cloud in May '22. Since joining Willie Mullins, he has won 4 times over hurdles, including at Grade 3 level. He looks the class act here, and with Colin Keane booked, he is the likely winner.
Ran green and didn't have the clearest run through on debut last time. Expected to improve for that first run and has cheekpieces on for the first time.

Plenty to like about his racecourse debut at Gowran at the beginning of September when a close 2nd in a 7f maiden, staying on late in the day. Not disgraced on his return at Cork last time, over a mile, when a close up 5th in a big field maiden. Further improvement is likely and holds decent claims if staying this much longer trip.

ran a lot better than might have been expected given an SP of 125/1 when making his racecourse debut in a mile maiden at the Curragh last month, finishing 10th of 18. Was doing his best work late and has improved on that run on his last two starts at Gowran and Tipperary, finishing 4th on both occasions. The way he’s been finishing off his races suggests there is more to come and is interesting here in first time cheekpieces.
Has only had one previous run on the flat. Not a bad effort over an inadequate trip. Price looks too big, now upped in trip and is worth a small each-way interest here.
Light Up The Dark is having its debut on the flat after winning two bumpers over 2 miles at Naas. Then followed that up over 2 miles 50 yards at Limerick, so has to have a great chance in this race.
Raced over an inadequate trip on reappearance run last time and moves back up in trip here. Will have tightened up for that run and should do better here.

Unlucky not to win on debut, the filly met trouble in running and jockey stated that Navy Waters shied away from the kickback of the soft ground. Goes up in trip today, and in a weak maiden, this looks like a good opportunity to open her account.
Probably needed the run when finishing 3rd on reappearance at Tipperary last month. Likely to be fitter for having had that run and should be there or thereabouts.

WASITTHEWAY could be the value play for a small yard. Maybe this three year old surprised connetions with how well he ran at huge odds when reappearing last month and so from a modest looking opening handicap mark he could show up well.

Having raced 3 times without a victory, she placed 15th out of 17 in her last outing at Cork, where she was a 150/1 outsider. With an increase in distance, this could be ideal for her first handicap race. Wes Joyce, who has achieved one win and 5 places from 6 rides at this venue, will have the reins. His 5lb claim makes the 16/1 odds for an each-way bet even more enticing.

Former pointer Game On has been placed in his last two maiden hurdles, including last time over course and distance, where he tried to make all but had nothing left when the winner went past, and he finished third. But this looks easier.
of significant interest now stepping back up in trip. has shaped well in the 2 runs for cromwell over inadequate trips. Looks a good thing here nudged up a couple of pounds

Our Zebo is one of only two that Noel Kelly has sent to Downpatrick from his base in Derry. This is by far his best chance, and he usually picks up a winner at this meeting. Ran well here when second on sole visit to this track, then followed it up with a clear-cut 11-length success next time out at Tramore. Has to shoulder a penalty, but this doesn't look the strongest race. NAP.

Mother Ship should get much closer to easy winner Our Zebo on twelve pounds better terms than when they were 1st and 2nd at Tramore last time and she may even turn the tables if she needed that race after a break of 177 days.

It wasn’t all that long ago that John McConnell was sending out Cheltenham winners, but it’s fair to say the yard has hit a rough patch. That said, his eight-year-old gelding TECHNOLOGY could offer a bit of hope here. This son of YEATS now finds himself 2lbs below the mark of his best run, which came on stable debut at Wexford (20f, good/yielding), where he finished second just 3¾ lengths behind the winner under today’s jockey, Ben Harvey. His subsequent run at Bellewstown (24f, good) wasn’t without promise; he was still travelling well at the 22f mark before fading late. The drop back in both trip and class today looks like a logical move. Trainer and jockey both have solid records in Northern Ireland, with McConnell boasting a 37.18% place strike rate over the last five years, and Harvey not far behind with 29.85% over the same period. Admittedly, I’d prefer to see a slightly bigger price, but TECHNOLOGY stood out on paper as one potentially well-treated at current ratings. A solid each-way case can be made.

SHE'LL BE KEPT shaped like a mare who would appreciate a stiffer test when racing in the handicap sphere. She comes from a shrewd yard who have multiple horses entered up in the coming days which reads well and she has nothing to fear from her opening mark. Maybe the market can help us.

The Real Screamer managed to win its last two starts last season over 1 mile 2 furlongs in handicaps on the all-weather at Dundalk. This season, it finished 3rd on its only start on soft ground at Navan, beaten 7 3/4 lengths. It should improve for that run, and the better ground should see The Real Screamer get back to winning ways.
Was well beaten on his first two starts but wasn't beaten too far when finishing sixth over 1m at Bellewstown last month. Step up in trip should suit. Should be thereabouts.
Has had three quick runs in maidens for connections and has shown ability to give hope for the future. Drops into claiming company here and has the scope to do better so no forlorn hope.
Showed some promise in 4 starts to date and finished 3rd of 11 on the latest outing. Makes first start for new yard and holds an each-way chance if finding improvement.

Impressive Bumper winner more than a year ago and was seen out only once more last year. Obviously had issues, but made a pleasing reappearance run last month when 2nd in a similar race as today. Should be winning this

Ian Donaghue is a trainer on the upgrade and has had success at this track recently. With the talented Darragh O'Keefe in my the plate they can guide this gelding to go one better than last time when finishing 35 lengths clear of the 3rd
Showed improvement last time staying in nicely over a shorter trip so this step up looks sure to suit. Good each way opportunity at a decent price.

Person Of Interest has only one point on his record where he was 2nd, beaten a neck, compared to Jollie Cosmos, who has run in two chases and ten points with lots of 2nds and 3rds. But she has not looked like winning. Even giving away lumps of weight, he should hold her on the run-in.

In the first time tongue tie and the master Keith Donaghue back in the saddle and perhaps a bit of an application of cash could see significant improvement in the jumping of this horse on handicap chase debut. Has talent as he won a maiden on decent ground last summer and today could be the day to strike over fences

Showed some promise on his racecourse debut over a mile at Gowran, finishing in midfield without having too hard a race. Ran a similar race back there last time when again finishing in midfield. Can hopefully improve enough to feature.
Has shown ability in her three starts and looked as though the run was needed last time at Bellewstown over 8f. She can hopefully do better here in first-time blinkers.
Has shown some promise in 2 starts to date without troubling the principals. Holds an each-way chance if finding expected improvement.

Placed 9th among 12 in a maiden event at Naas 11 days prior. While lacking competitiveness in 3 races, this 3 year old has shown promise. With Sheridan as the jockey, the 22/1 odds offer great value in this open race.
